text: Anomaly detection isn't a new pipeline stage — it's a statistical way to ask whether a value is unusual given everything you've seen, sharper than a fixed hardcoded threshold.
Z-score assumes your metric is roughly normally distributed and flags anything more than about three standard deviations from the mean — a cheap, common first check on daily row counts.
Z-score's catch is its normal-distribution assumption. Isolation forest makes no such assumption, handles multiple metrics at once, and flags points that separate out in just a few random splits.

An LLM doesn't replace either method — it helps draft the z-score check as code or explain a flagged result in plain language. The statistics decide what's anomalous; AI speeds up the writing and explaining.
Sharper than a hardcoded threshold, still grounded in real statistics. Next up: using an LLM to draft automated data documentation.
